messages:
Ana Patel: Hey team — need to lock the POC plan for Acme Health (enterprise). They want a 2-week POC starting Mon May 12. Success criteria they gave: p95 latency < 300ms for 512 tokens, embedding similarity >= 0.86 on 5 eval sets, no data leaves VPC, and a rough cost estimate under $5k for the POC. Need SE/eng + ML support. Who can own infra/setup, prompt evals, and security?
Mike Chen: I can own infra/setup. Will need dedicated instance + VPC peering + KMS. Requesting 2xA100-equivalent GPUs or equivalent throughput. Which model are we supposed to validate?
Ana Patel: Client prefers an open LLM — proposed model is a 70B quantized variant (customer callout). If that won't fit latency budget we fallback to a 30B quantized.
deploy-bot: Dedicated instance r-inference-acme-782 provision request queued. ETA provisioning: ~48h.
Jess Rivera: I’ll lead prompt engineering and the eval harness. I need a sample dataset (1000 queries) + golden labels. Can Acme share by Wed? Also will scaffold tests for answer accuracy, hallucination checks, and extraction precision.
Riyad Khan: I’ll take quality baselines and embedding thresholds. Quick Q: are we using cosine similarity or dot product for embeddings? Also we should pin model version + quant profile in the SOW.
Sara Lopez: Security note — they require completed security questionnaire + SOC2 attestation and audit log access. Need to confirm KMS key policy for customer-managed keys. I’ll own the SQA.
Tom Nguyen: From eng/runtime: I can help with batching config, KV cache tuning, and rollout/fallback variants. For p95 latency we should start with batch_size=16, prefer low-latency kernel path. Need expected QPS pattern.
Ana Patel: Proposed timeline (nominal):
- Day 0 (Mon): kickoff call + NDA signed
- Day 2: infra provisioned & VPC peered
- Day 4: integration + smoke tests
- Day 8: run eval harness + embeddings baseline
- Day 12: iterate on prompts/models, final smoke
- Day 14: POC review & decision
Is that realistic?
Mike Chen: Provisioning + peering + KMS often takes ~48h, so Day 2 might be optimistic. Realistic: kickoff Mon, infra ready Wed EOD, integration Thu-Fri. If Acme can pre-share network CIDRs and KMS info today we can shave time.
Jess Rivera: That works. I’ll scaffold the harness this week and run a smoke by Fri. I’ll post the prompt set in #eng-ml for review.
Riyad Khan: For embeddings: I’ll set initial threshold at cosine >= 0.86 and run on their 5 eval subsets. Need S3 path access to results and logs. Please grant role redwood-poc-acme with read/write to s3://acme-poc.
Sara Lopez: Also need confirmation whether dataset contains PHI. Client says no PHI but may have pseudonyms. I’ll run DLP scans regardless and redact if policy flags.
Ana Patel: I’ll confirm dataset content with Acme and send NDA + security questionnaire. Pricing note: 2-week POC offered complimentary; if they want reserved capacity after POC we’ll provide a pro-rated quote. Any objections?
Mike Chen: No objections.
Tom Nguyen: All good from eng. One ask: add a fallback model (smaller) in the rollout policy to avoid outages during stress tests.
Jess Rivera: Agreed. I’ll include fallback scenarios in the eval matrix.
Ana Patel: Action items — I’ll update the SOW and send kickoff calendar invite.
- @Mike Chen: provision instance + confirm VPC/KMS by Wed EOD
- @Jess Rivera: scaffold eval harness + smoke by Fri
- @Riyad Khan: run baselines and thresholds by Mon of week 2
- @Sara Lopez: start SQA + DLP scan once dataset available
I’ll post customer sample queries here when received. :thumbsup:
Mike Chen: Will ping network team now and open peering ticket (ticket #NET-4891).
Riyad Khan: Once access is granted I’ll drop a minimal runbook for how to push test data and where to find logs.
Sara Lopez: I’ll attach the SQA checklist to the SOW draft.
Ana Patel: Thanks all — I’ll confirm kickoff with Acme and flag any blockers. If anything slips we regroup Tuesday.
Tom Nguyen: 👍
Jess Rivera: 👍
